newsitem.title: USA: Jet fuel weakens in NYH, bearish stock data seen.
newsitem.headline: Jet fuel weakens in NYH, bearish stock data seen.

text.p: Jet fuel differentials eased in the New York Harbor Tuesday amid expectations that oil inventory data expected out this afternoon will suggest the region's higher year over year supply is growing.

"There are millions of more barrels more now than last year (in the Harbor region), and the only reason jet fuel is holding up even this much is the falling outright price. Otherwise, we are expecting distillates to build yet again," said a New York Harbor dealer.

NYMEX July heating oil ended up 0.15 cent at 51.65 cents a gallon. Still, July heat has lost 4.82 cents in the previous five sessions, making the futures price more in line with spot supply and thus narrowing the differential.

Low sulphur jet fuel in the New York Harbor was offered at 2.25 cents over NYMEX July heating oil versus 2.40 cents Monday. In the U.S. Gulf, the prompt airline quality 54 grade differential was unchanged with Monday, offered at 0.50 cent under July heating oil.
Tuesday evening, the American Petroleum Institute (API) is expected by traders to report a 2.5 million barrel increase in distillate stocks.
Heating oil, like other distillates, can be turned into jet fuel. The API said jet fuel stocks as of May 30 were four million barrels above a year ago in the U.S. Northeast.
Tonight's API report reflects the week ended June 6.
